data.description:
## Problem

`pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` carries `timeout_func_only = true` (added by story
`bold-abeyant-indri`, commit `6a5c88027c5`). pytest-timeout documents that key as deferring
"the timeout evaluation to only the test function body, **ignoring the time it takes when
evaluating any fixtures used in the test**" (`pytest_timeout.py:150-152`).

So setup and teardown are now **unguarded** by the per-test hang budget.

That is the exact phase the guard was originally built for. Bug `balsamy-eloquent-iggypops`
(89d5-61da-b621-47f8) was filed because the `ubuntu-latest, py3.11` cell went silent at 99% and
burned the full 60-minute job cap; the mechanism its RCA proved (recorded in that ticket and
carried into `digestive-purposeful-quagga` / 4a11-aecf-4d33-45ae) was a `with TestClient(app)`
that entered the review-bot lifespan and awaited `queue.join()` under a 1200 s
`shutdown_drain_seconds()` **on context exit** — i.e. in teardown. The guard 89d5 landed
(`--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`, no `func_only`) covered all phases and would bound
that. The current ini would not.

This was NOT the cause of the worker crashes in `soppy-logophilic-husky`, and it was deliberately
left untouched by that fix (which restores the budget to 300 and changes nothing else, since the
crash cost was all `call` time). It is filed separately so the coverage gap is not lost.

## Why it is not simply reverted

`func_only` has a real motivation: without it a slow session-scoped fixture can spend an
individual test's allowance, and the ini now applies to bare local `pytest` and `make test` as
well as CI, where session fixtures are not amortised the same way. Dropping the key outright
would newly bound local fixture setup and could red the suite for reasons unrelated to hangs.

## Suggested approach (to be confirmed by whoever claims this)

Options, cheapest first:

1. Add `session_timeout` (pytest-timeout's whole-session ceiling, `pytest_timeout.py:108`) so a
   fixture hang is still bounded somewhere, without charging it to a single test.
2. Drop `timeout_func_only` and measure whether any fixture actually approaches the 300 s budget
   — if none does, the key is buying nothing and its cost is real.
3. Keep `func_only` but add a targeted guard for the specific known-dangerous shape: a fixture
   or assertion that fails fast when a test enters the review-bot lifespan without the
   `reconcile_loop` stub (this is the same insurance `digestive-purposeful-quagga` proposes).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test whose SETUP or TEARDOWN hangs is bounded and names itself, rather than running to
      the 60-minute job cap; demonstrated by an out-of-process nested-pytest arm in the style of
      `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py`'s negative arm.
- [ ] Whatever is chosen does not re-introduce the problem `func_only` was added to solve: a slow
      shared fixture must not expire an individual test; demonstrated by a second arm.
- [ ] The chosen configuration is recorded in `pyproject.toml` with a comment citing this ticket
      and 89d5-61da-b621-47f8.
data.title: timeout_func_only leaves fixture setup/teardown hangs unguarded
